title: Scientists May Have Discovered a Massive Starless Galaxy

claims.claim: Cold dark matter physicists think makes up about 85 percent of the universe's matter.

evidence.quote: cold dark matter, a hypothetical substance that physicists think makes up about 85 percent of the universe’s matter.

claims.claim: Researchers published their findings regarding a dark galaxy candidate in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society.

evidence.quote: Now, researchers have found a promising candidate for such a dark galaxy and published their findings in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society.

claims.claim: The object known as AGC 322753 contains roughly 2 billion times the sun's mass in hydrogen.

evidence.quote: The object, known as AGC 322753, contains roughly 2 billion times the sun's mass in hydrogen, yet appears to have no stars

claims.claim: Researchers at Swinburne University of Technology in Australia made the discovery by comparing observations from two existing radio surveys.

evidence.quote: Researchers at Swinburne University of Technology in Australia made the discovery by comparing observations from two existing radio surveys

claims.claim: One radio survey was conducted by the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico and the other by China's Five-Hundred-Meter Aperture Spherical Radio Telescope.

evidence.quote: one conducted by the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico and the other by China's Five-Hundred-Meter Aperture Spherical Radio Telescope.

claims.claim: Marco Monaci is an author of the study at Swinburne University of Technology.

evidence.quote: "The theoretical models and the simulations show us that dark galaxies shouldn't rotate, so this is extremely interesting," says Marco Monaci, an author of the study at Swinburne University of Technology.

claims.claim: Deep optical images from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys reveal no starlight for AGC 322753.

evidence.quote: even deep optical images from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, which search for starlight rather than the hydrogen gas detected by radio telescopes, reveal none.

claims.claim: The team estimates that AGC 322753 contains at least 40 times more mass in hydrogen than in stars.

evidence.quote: From this, the team estimates that AGC322753 contains at least 40 times more mass in hydrogen than in stars
